Approximately one year ago, Dr. Liu made changes to one of my teeth using a spring Hawley retainer without discussing the change with me or asking for my consent. If she had simply asked whether I wanted that tooth adjusted, I would have said no because I was satisfied with its position.

Instead, the retainer pushed my tooth backward, and I have now been dealing with pain in that tooth for an entire year. In addition to the physical discomfort, I have spent significant time traveling back and forth to appointments, paying for Uber rides, rearranging my schedule, and waiting for the issue to be corrected.

To make matters more concerning, another orthodontist in the same office told me that my tooth was fine and that he would not have made the adjustment that Dr. Liu made. That only reinforced my belief that this unnecessary change could have been avoided.

After I brought my concerns to the office manager, they agreed to remake my retainer. However, when I arrived for my appointment today—after taking the time to travel to the office—I was informed that the new retainer had been lost. Instead of informing me in advance, the office waited until 8:30 PM the night before my appointment to email me that I would owe $470, even with insurance.

When I called the next morning, I was told the charge was primarily for X-rays. I asked if I could provide recent X-rays from my previous dentist, and I was told that would be acceptable. However, my original appointment was at 9:30 AM—the same time my previous dentist’s office opened—making it impossible to obtain them beforehand. Initially, I was told my appointment could not be moved, and staff claimed I had only provided my insurance information three days earlier, which was not true. I had provided my insurance information multiple times and had been waiting months for this appointment.

After speaking with the office manager, she rescheduled my appointment to 7:00 PM and told me she would contact my previous dentist to obtain my X-rays. I appreciated her willingness to help at the time.

Unfortunately, that effort never materialized. I ultimately obtained the X-rays myself and sent them to the office, but I was then told they were not sufficient and that I would still need new X-rays. The office offered a 20% discount, but I would still have been responsible for approximately $155 out of pocket.

The biggest issue for me wasn’t the cost—it was the lack of communication and follow-through. I spent considerable time trying to resolve this in advance, made multiple phone calls, obtained my own records, and still ended up without a workable solution. After this experience, I decided to cancel my appointment.

I understand that diagnostic requirements and insurance coverage can vary, but patients deserve clear communication, accurate information, and follow-through on commitments. The hygienist was great (she actually took the time to give me a mini consultation on my brushing habits) and answered all my initial concerns. They were also quick about confirming my insurance and transferring info from my previous dentist, and they were upfront and clear about what the visit would cost. And potentially what else they might do and what my insurance showed I was eligible for.

Dr. Pham was amazing. He was informative and patiently answered all of my questions. What I appreciated most was how honest he was. I’ve been to several dentists in the past where you can just tell the practice is trying to maximize $$$$$ revenue (and push unnecessary work), but yah it seems like Dr. Pham genuinely wants what is best.

The manager Stephaine stopped responding to my texts and follow ups altogether.
